edit.description: the one-path-per-line fact, which declares the shape it cannot carry and refuses on nothing
beside the case that already drives a real declared gate's child and reads its environment back

summary: a touched path carrying a newline splits into two lines of `FLUME_TOUCHED_PATHS`, and the site that declares the gap names no refusal
acceptance: a declared command gate whose span touched a path the one-path-per-line channel cannot spell refuses naming that path, and a span of spellable paths reaches its child's environment exactly as it does today
tests: a declared command gate refuses a span whose touched path carries a newline
pins: a declared command gate's touched-paths fact carries one line per path of a span the channel can spell
notes: harness/declaredGates.ts:148 joins on newline and its block names the unspellable shape — "a tracked path containing a newline is the one shape this channel cannot spell" — with nothing downstream refusing, so a gate keying files reads two paths that are not in the span. Reachable: the engine decodes `touchedPaths` from git's NUL-delimited output, which preserves one. The env channel cannot carry a NUL, so the refusal is the fix rather than a second encoding.
